videos.title: What is Langsys? Your app in every language, no redeploy
videos.summary:
Langsys in 77 seconds: an SDK in your app and a hosted Translation Manager. A phrase registers itself the first time your code runs it, is machine-translated on arrival, and can be refined by a translator without a deploy.

The proof: a blog post published at 09:00, with no build and no write key, reaches a reader in Madrid in Spanish at 09:03.

videos.title: Getting started with Langsys, end to end
videos.summary: One take from nothing to a translated app: create the project and its languages, create an API key, install and initialise the SDK, and watch t(), ‹Translate›, ‹Phrase› and ‹DontTranslate› register their phrases. The Spanish is already in the Translation Manager, and the app switches to Spanish and French with no reload.

videos.title: Plurals in every language, without if (count === 1)
videos.summary: Why a sentence changes with its number, why the if (count === 1) that fixes it in English is English grammar living in your code, and how writing the sentence flat gets you every plural form in every language. Langsys translates it flat, then rebuilds it in each locale's own ICU plural categories, English included.

videos.title: The translation pipeline, and how Langsys deletes it
videos.summary: Concepts 1 of 5. Translation usually round-trips through a pipeline: extract, export, translate, import, deploy. Langsys removes it.

videos.title: No more key files: the sentence is the key
videos.summary: Concepts 2 of 5. Where a project starts, the key other i18n libraries make you invent, and what replaces it in Langsys.

videos.title: The locale store: holding and switching the active language
videos.summary: Concepts 3 of 5. How Langsys holds the active locale and switches it across your app.

videos.title: API keys and environments: which key goes where
videos.summary: Concepts 4 of 5. Why a key that can register phrases can never ship, why read-only is a dead end, and what ip_write is: one key whose answer depends on where you ask from. Write keys stay on machines you own, ip_write goes into any public bundle, and read-only is for bundles that must never change anything.

videos.title: Adding a new language is a project setting
videos.summary: Concepts 5 of 5. Reaching a new language is a setting, not a project: new phrases translate on arrival, and one run fills in the rest.

videos.hold: Filmed against translation-manager MR !1; until it ships, Send on the invite dialog errors on the live app.
videos.title: Managing translations in the Langsys Translation Manager
videos.summary: The Translation Manager for whoever owns the copy, with no code on screen: the to-do list, a machine draft corrected by hand, AI Translate with Auto-next, Never Translate, and a translator invited to Spanish only. The correction is live in the app with nothing deployed.

videos.title: Translation memory: a new project that starts already translated
videos.summary: A second project in the same organization opens fully translated before anyone touches it. Translation memory carries every sentence, and who wrote it, across projects, so no model is called for the new project at all.

videos.title: Use Langsys from Claude Code over MCP
videos.summary: Langsys inside an AI assistant, over the hosted MCP server: one claude mcp add command, approval in the browser, and Claude Code answering questions about your project's languages from live data. The connection can be revoked from your account's Security tab.

videos.title: Add German to a live app: exact quote, no deploy
videos.summary: German added to a live store. Langsys quotes the existing catalog exactly before anything runs (29 words, $0.35), translates it, and the store switches to German with nothing built or deployed.

videos.title: Catching up a language that fell behind
videos.summary: Bulk actions in the Translation Manager: AI Translate Pending for one language or the whole project, with a confirmation that lists every target locale and its cost, and every language back to complete.

videos.hold: Filmed against translation-manager MR !2; until it ships, the live app drops a segment edit and needs a reload to show the AI result.
videos.title: Translating a whole content block as one
videos.summary: A ‹Translate› region translated as one content block: AI Translate fills every segment together, a segment is rewritten by hand in the formal register, and a ‹DontTranslate› sentence stays in English while the Italian is filled in around it.

videos.title: AI Translator settings, every switch explained
videos.summary: The AI Translator tab top to bottom: AI translations on demand, auto-translate for new phrases, and auto-detect holding a phrase that arrives already in Spanish as never-translate.

videos.title: API keys in production: activity, pausing and rotation
videos.summary: A key after it ships: a real week of storefront traffic on its Activity page, pausing a key without deleting it, and rotation on camera: the three key types, a new IP write key created with an allowlist, and the old one deleted.

videos.title: One organization, many projects
videos.summary: The organization as the thing every project starts from: default locales, AI Translator and billing settings, project funding from the organization's balance, and a customized project switched back to inheriting.

videos.title: Usage and credits: how a project gets funded
videos.summary: The two meters, API usage units and credits, and how a project gets funded: a credit transfer from the account to a project done on camera, one line per machine translation in its history, and the project's monthly limit and auto recharge.

videos.title: Plans and payments in Langsys
videos.summary: A tour of billing with nothing submitted: the plan and billing cycle, the Change Plan dialog, payment methods shared with an organization or project, addresses, and invoices.

videos.title: Notifications: what Langsys tells you, and where
videos.summary: The notifications inbox and its settings: account defaults for new phrases, invitations and project access, by in-app and email, and a per-project override.

videos.title: Svelte i18n with Langsys: the full walkthrough
videos.summary: What other i18n makes you keep in step, one call to replace it, a locale switch, why flat Spanish is wrong for half your users, and what ICU select does about it.

videos.title: t(phrase, category, params) in Svelte
videos.summary: The t() call: the keys-file problem it replaces, its three arguments, ICU placeholders and plurals.

videos.title: ‹Phrase› in Svelte: a sentence with markup inside
videos.summary: A sentence with markup inside it, kept as one phrase, and why ‹Phrase› params are written %name%.

videos.title: ‹Translate› in Svelte: one tag for a whole region
videos.summary: One ‹Translate› tag registers a whole region, and why a block beats a call per line.

videos.title: ‹DontTranslate› in Svelte: keep brand names verbatim
videos.summary: Brand names and identifiers held back verbatim, without hoisting them out of the sentence.

videos.title: What is a content block? Translating a whole section in Svelte
videos.summary: One section registered as a unit, still made of individually reusable phrases.

videos.title: Same word, two meanings: categories instead of i18n keys
videos.summary: Why i18n invented keys, and what replaces them: the same word with two meanings, and the pairs it splits into.

videos.title: Gender agreement without conditionals in your code (ICU select)
videos.summary: The gender conditional other i18n leaves in your component, and the branches Langsys generates for each language instead.

videos.title: Translating placeholders, alt text and aria labels in Svelte
videos.summary: What a half-translated form looks like to the person using it, and how one ‹Translate› reaches placeholders, alt text and aria labels in the same pass.

videos.title: Numbers and dates in every locale with Svelte i18n
videos.summary: Numbers and dates per CLDR: the branch you'd write by hand, why digit grouping is a shape and not a separator, and why an order number must be passed as a string.

videos.title: Your i18n key is just the English sentence #Shorts
videos.summary: With Langsys the sentence in your code is the translation key: no keys file, nothing to extract or keep in sync, and the same line comes back in every language. #Shorts

videos.title: Bienvenido or Bienvenida? One line of code #Shorts
videos.summary: Spanish agrees with the user. Langsys generates the ICU select branches, so Diego gets Bienvenido, Laura gets Bienvenida, and an unknown gender gets the neutral form, from one line. #Shorts

videos.title: Russian has 4 plural forms. You write one line #Shorts
videos.summary: One, few, many and other: Russian picks a plural form by the number, and 21 goes back to the singular. Write the sentence flat and Langsys builds every form each locale needs. #Shorts

videos.title: Translate a whole section with one tag #Shorts
videos.summary: One Translate tag wraps a region of markup: every run of text becomes its own phrase, bold and links land where they belong, and the brand name is never translated. #Shorts

videos.title: Published at 09:00, read in Spanish at 09:03 #Shorts
videos.summary: A blog post goes live with no build and no deploy. Its first reader's app sends Langsys only the page address, Langsys reads the page itself, and minutes later a reader in Madrid gets it in Spanish. #Shorts

videos.title: Ask your AI assistant how your translations are doing #Shorts
videos.summary: Langsys hosts an MCP server, so Claude, Codex, Cursor or GitHub Copilot can read your projects and translate what's missing. One approval in your browser, and the assistant never sees your password. #Shorts

videos.title: A brand-new project that starts already translated #Shorts
videos.summary: Fix a translation once and every new project in your organization starts out knowing it. Translation Memory filled this project in Spanish, with the original translator's credit, and no model was called. #Shorts

videos.title: In Spanish, the bold moves to where it belongs #Shorts
videos.summary: Other i18n cuts a sentence with a bold word into three keys. With ‹Phrase› the translator gets one sentence, markup and all, and in Spanish the bold lands after the noun, on "no leídos". #Shorts

videos.title: Add German to a live store, with no deploy #Shorts
videos.summary: Add the language in your project settings, not in your code. Langsys quotes the exact price for the existing catalog before it spends anything, drafts every phrase in seconds, and the store speaks German with nothing built or deployed. #Shorts

videos.title: Two languages behind, caught up in one action #Shorts
videos.summary: French and Japanese were each missing two phrases. AI Translate Pending drafts them in seconds, and the drafts wait for someone to review them. #Shorts

videos.title: Your brand name, never translated #Shorts
videos.summary: A translator can't tell a product name from a phrase, so other i18n ships Bright Ledger as Libro Mayor Brillante. With Langsys you mark it where it stands with ‹DontTranslate›, and the sentence around it still translates. #Shorts

videos.title: One English word, two Spanish translations #Shorts
videos.summary: "Free" is a price on one screen and an empty evening on another. Other i18n invents a key to tell them apart. Langsys keeps the sentence and files it under a category: Gratis and Libre. #Shorts

videos.title: Placeholders and alt text translate too #Shorts
videos.summary: Other i18n needs a separate call on every attribute, and the one you forget stays English. One ‹Translate› tag covers the region: the placeholder, the image description and the label a screen reader announces. #Shorts

videos.title: Every number and date in each locale's format #Shorts
videos.summary: Pass the number itself and the date as a date: German gets 1.234,5 and 14. März 2026, and Hindi groups 1234567 as 12,34,567. An order number goes in as a string, so it stays exactly as written. #Shorts
